title: Nonparametric tail estimator and dashboard for p95/p99 by route/model/region
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Add a robust, low-noise p95/p99 estimation pipeline and an interactive dashboard that slices latency by route, model, and region. The feature combines a nonparametric tail estimator with reservoir sampling and slice-aware sketches so we can display high-fidelity percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec overlays without storing full request lists. This work also adds regression detection using sequential hypothesis testing and integrates alerts into our existing runbooks.
background: Current percentile dashboards rely on coarse rollups that under-report tail spikes from low-volume routes and small regional partitions. Existing heuristics produce noisy alerts and high false positives during diurnal load swings. We've observed missed regressions on dedicated capacity customers where model variants increase per-token latency by 10-25% in p99 but aggregate metrics hide the shift.
goals: Produce stable p95 and p99 estimates for any (route, model, region) slice with limited memory and CPU overhead
Expose tokens/sec alongside percentiles to correlate throughput and tail behavior
Implement regression detectors that surface sustained percentile shifts (tunable sensitivity) and integrate with Alerting and Rollouts
Ship an interactive dashboard with drilldowns, confidence bands, and attribution links to PRs/rollouts
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for selected route/model/region over ranges 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d
Estimates for p95/p99 have median absolute error < 3% vs ground-truth from replay for slices with >=100 requests/hour
Regression detector triggers on synthetic and historical replayed regressions with <5% false positive rate during normal diurnal patterns
System emits quantile-change events to the pipeline topic and a Slack/PagerDuty alert when configured
CPU and memory overhead on telemetry workers limits: additional 8% CPU, +150MB per worker at peak for 5000 active slices
design_decisions: Estimator: Harrell-Davis style nonparametric quantile estimator combined with reservoir sampling for very small slices
Sketching: t-digest for streaming bulk slices (>=1k reqs/window) and GK for tight memory-constrained slices
Detection: sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) on the p95 time-series with adaptive windowing and baselining to reduce diurnal false positives
Throughput: tokens/sec computed as a derived metric from accepted request samples and decayed counters to avoid double counting streaming chunks
Storage: only keep aggregated sketches per 1m bucket retained for 7d (configurable) to satisfy retention / memory targets
implementation_tasks: Telemetry worker: add Harrell-Davis + reservoir sampler implementation and tests
Sketch library: integrate updated t-digest variant (merge-friendly) and GK fallback
Aggregation pipeline: emit per-1m sketches into telemetry topic with metadata (route, model, region, seq_len_profile)
Regression engine: implement SPRT module with tunable alpha/beta and auto-baseline feature
Dashboard: build new panels (quantile ribbons, tokens/sec overlay, attribution table) in Console
Load harness: create synthetic traffic generator that can replay historical sequences and inject controlled latency shifts
Alerting: wire quantile-change events into alerting service with runbook links
monitoring_queries: quantile_estimator_error{slice=~".*"} - computes median absolute error vs replay ground-truth
telemetry_worker_cpu_percent - CPU impact on telemetry workers
dashboard_panels: Time-series: p50/p95/p99 with 95% confidence band (per selected slice)
Heatmap: tokens/sec vs p95 (routes on y-axis, time on x-axis) for selected model
Attribution table: top drivers of p95 change (route, model, region, recent PR link)
Slice explorer: distribution histogram with t-digest previews and sample-count histogram
Regression timeline: detected regression events with severity and link to runbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for estimator math (edge cases: all identical latencies, heavily skewed tails)
Replay tests: run historical 30-day replay across sampled routes and verify estimator error targets
Synthetic regression tests: inject +20% and +40% p99 deltas for 30m and 6h windows and verify detection
Load test: run telemetry workers under 10k active slices to measure CPU/memory impact
Canary rollout: enable pipeline for telemetry-candidate region with read-only dashboard then opt-in alerting
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy estimator to telemetry-candidate region, enable dashboards in read-only mode (2 days)
Phase 2 (opt-in alerts): allow 3 internal teams to enable regression alerts and collect feedback (1 week)
Phase 3 (global): flip default on for all hosted regions and enable alerting with conservative thresholds (2 weeks), then tighten thresholds after 1 week
Fallback: switch to aggregated t-digest-only path if telemetry worker resource usage exceeds threshold
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives during traffic spikes. Mitigation: SPRT with adaptive baseline and minimum sample-count gating
Risk: memory blow-up with many tiny slices. Mitigation: reservoir sampling and TTL-based pruning of sub-slices
Risk: estimator mismatch vs replay due to sampling bias. Mitigation: periodic full-replay comparisons and calibration job
Risk: alerts overwhelm on rollout. Mitigation: staged enablement and alert rate-limiting with dedup windows
